sheets.lifecycle: Read once at session start, then applies to every turn of that session. Changing or switching the style takes effect only after /clear or a new session, and switching it invalidates the prompt cache. It stops applying when outputStyle is changed back or the session ends.
sheets.failure_mode: Advisory. The style shapes the system prompt but does not validate output, so Claude can drift out of the table format on a long or unusual turn, and there is no hook-free way to catch that; if the format is contractual, add a Stop or PostToolUse check. Two quieter failures: dropping the coding instructions also drops the built-in guidance on scoping changes and verifying work, which matters if the annotation project ever touches code; and a teammate who edited the style mid-session sees no change until /clear.
sheets.version_caveat: No plan restriction. The standalone /output-style command was deprecated in v2.1.73 and removed in v2.1.91, so drive it from /config or the outputStyle setting. Nested project output-style directories resolve closest-to-working-directory from v2.1.178. If you later ship the style in a plugin, force-for-plugin applies it automatically and overrides the user's outputStyle setting, with the first loaded plugin winning when several set it.

sheets.primary: An output style, configured at project level so it is active for the whole project, replacing the default software-engineering framing with a data-analyst persona and a fixed tabular reply format. Output styles are the mechanism that removes default behaviour rather than adding to it, which is the specific requirement here.
sheets.rejected_alternative: CLAUDE.md instructions describing the persona and the format, rejected because CLAUDE.md appends to the existing system framing and cannot remove the default engineering behaviour, so the model keeps drifting back to it.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The model. The style is prompt text and the format compliance is a behavioural property, though the harness owns which style is selected and keeps it selected across turns.
sheets.context_boundary: The main interactive session's system framing, applied to every turn rather than injected once. It does not automatically govern subagent contexts or headless invocations, so a spawned subagent may answer in the default engineering voice unless separately configured.
sheets.lifecycle: Applies from the moment the style is selected, persists across turns and sessions for as long as the setting stands, and stops when the style is switched back or the project setting is removed.
sheets.failure_mode: Advisory with gradual drift: over a long session, and especially after a tool-heavy stretch or an error, the model slips back toward prose and engineering behaviour, and nothing validates that a reply actually matches the tabular schema. If strict conformance matters, add a check outside the model rather than trusting the style, and be aware the style also suppresses helpful default behaviours that the team may miss.
sheets.version_caveat: Output styles were added in a 2025 release and the surrounding surface has kept moving, including built-in styles and the newer overlap with plugin-supplied personas; I cannot state the exact minimum version or whether project-level selection is supported on the team's build, so verify before assuming every session in the project picks it up.

scenarios.scenario: Every time the agent modifies a TypeScript file, our formatter must run on that file. We wrote the instruction into the project guidance the agent reads at startup, but every few sessions it skips the step and unformatted code lands in a commit.

key.primary: PostToolUse hook with an Edit|Write matcher whose command runs the formatter on the edited file path
key.rejected_alternative: A CLAUDE.md instruction telling Claude to always run the formatter after editing
key.rejection_reason: The memory docs state CLAUDE.md is context, not enforced configuration, with no guarantee of strict compliance, and explicitly say that anything that must run at a specific point, such as after each file edit, should be written as a hook, which executes at fixed lifecycle events regardless of what Claude decides.
key.context_boundary: no context window (the formatter is a shell process fired after each matching edit); by default nothing crosses into the conversation because for most hook events stdout goes to the debug log, and only a blocking exit 2 stderr or an explicit additionalContext return feeds anything back to Claude
key.lifecycle: PostToolUse event fires after each successful tool call whose tool name matches Edit|Write
key.failure_mode: A matcher typo or a failing script skips formatting silently, because non-blocking hook errors do not stop the session; the hook also runs on every matching edit whether or not the file needed formatting.

sheets.primary: A PostToolUse hook registered in the repository's .claude/settings.json, with matcher "Edit|Write", whose command reads .tool_input.file_path from the event JSON, filters for .ts/.tsx, and runs the formatter on that one path. The harness invokes the shell command at the lifecycle point, so the formatting step no longer depends on the model electing to do it.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Project guidance in CLAUDE.md or a .claude/rules file. That is exactly what is already in place and failing: memory files shape what the model tries to do but nothing checks that it did, so a skipped step is invisible until the commit lands.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. Claude Code runs hooks at fixed points in its own lifecycle, so the formatter runs whether or not the model remembered; the model contributes nothing except triggering the edit.
sheets.context_boundary: The hook runs outside the model's context window, as a separate process in the current directory with Claude Code's environment. Only the event JSON crosses in on stdin; only stderr or an additionalContext string crosses back into the conversation, capped at 10,000 characters.
sheets.lifecycle: Fires immediately after each successful Edit or Write tool call, in the main conversation and inside subagents, and stops when the hook entry is removed from settings. It does not fire for files Claude changes through Bash, nor for @-mentioned files, which are inserted without a tool call.
sheets.failure_mode: Advisory after the fact, and it fails open with respect to the write itself: PostToolUse cannot block, the file is already on disk when the hook fires, and a formatter that errors only shows stderr to Claude. It also misses any TypeScript file rewritten via Bash or codegen, so a Stop hook that scans the working tree once per turn is needed for full coverage.
sheets.version_caveat: No plan restriction, experimental status, or enabling flag applies. The pipe matcher "Edit|Write" works on every version; the comma form "Edit,Write" is only accepted on Claude Code v2.1.191 or later, so write the pipe form for a mixed fleet.

sheets.primary: A PostToolUse hook declared in the project's .claude/settings.json, matched on the file-editing tools (Write and Edit, plus MultiEdit if that tool name exists in your version), which reads the edited path from the hook's stdin JSON, filters for .ts/.tsx, and shells out to the formatter on exactly that file.
sheets.rejected_alternative: CLAUDE.md / project rules guidance, which is what is already in place and is exactly what fails: instructions in context are advisory and the model drops them under load.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. The hook is executed by Claude Code itself after the tool call, so the model's attention is not part of the guarantee.
sheets.context_boundary: The formatter runs in a separate OS process with no model context at all; only the tool-call JSON crosses out (tool name, file path, cwd, session id) and only the hook's exit code plus any stderr text crosses back into the model's context.
sheets.lifecycle: Fires on every successful matching edit, for every session started in that repo, from the moment the settings file is loaded at startup; it stops applying if the hook entry is removed, if the session is started outside the repo, or if hooks are disabled for the run.
sheets.failure_mode: It fails open in the ways that matter: if the formatter binary is missing or the hook errors and exits zero, the edit still stands unformatted, and the hook never sees writes made through Bash (sed, a codegen script, git apply), so those still land raw. Exiting non-zero with a message is what pushes the failure back to the model rather than swallowing it. It also cannot cover files changed by a process outside the agent, so a commit-time gate is still the belt to this suspenders.
sheets.version_caveat: Hook events and matchers are configured in settings.json and the matcher is a tool-name pattern, so the exact tool names to match (whether MultiEdit still exists as a distinct tool) depend on the CLI version; I cannot confirm the version number at which the edit tools were consolidated without the documentation, so the matcher should be verified against the installed build rather than copied.

sheets.primary: A PostToolUse hook committed in the repo's .claude/settings.json, matcher Edit|Write scoped with if: "Edit(*.ts)", whose command handler runs the formatter on tool_input.file_path. The harness runs it after every matching edit, so the model gets no opportunity to skip the step.
sheets.rejected_alternative: CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules guidance telling the agent to format after editing TypeScript. That is the mechanism already failing here: it is advisory context the model can and does drop.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. Claude Code fires the hook on the lifecycle event and runs the formatter itself, so neither the decision nor the execution belongs to the model.
sheets.context_boundary: The handler runs in its own OS process with the event JSON on stdin, outside the model's context window. Only the exit code and stdout JSON (additionalContext, systemMessage, capped at 10,000 characters) cross back into the session.
sheets.lifecycle: Fires immediately after each successful Edit or Write tool call, in the main session and inside subagents, for every session started in that repo. It stops when the entry is removed from settings or disableAllHooks is set at the same or a higher tier.
sheets.failure_mode: Corrective rather than preventive: the write has already landed, so the hook reformats after the fact and cannot block. If the model commits in the same turn before the reformat lands, unformatted bytes still reach the commit. A missing formatter or a crashed handler exits non-zero, which is a non-blocking error, so it fails open silently.
sheets.version_caveat: No version gate on PostToolUse itself. The comma form of the matcher (Edit,Write) needs v2.1.191 or later, and an if pattern like Edit(src/**) changed matching depth at v2.1.214. Avoid jq in the handler if any developer is on Windows without it installed.

sheets.primary: A PostToolUse hook in the project's .claude/settings.json with matcher "Edit|Write", narrowed with the handler-level "if": "Edit(**/*.ts)" field, running a command that reads .tool_input.file_path from the hook's stdin JSON and invokes the formatter on exactly that file. The hook replaces the startup instruction so the format step is executed by Claude Code rather than chosen by the model.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Keeping the rule in CLAUDE.md or a .claude/rules file, which is the configuration already in place: it is advisory context that shapes intent but never guarantees the step, which is why it is skipped every few sessions.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. Claude Code fires PostToolUse after every matching tool call regardless of whether the model remembered the convention, and the model has no say in whether the hook runs.
sheets.context_boundary: The hook runs in its own OS process outside the model's context window; the CLI passes tool_input, tool_response and duration_ms in on stdin. Only what the hook returns (a decision, reason, or additionalContext) crosses back, so the reformatted bytes on disk are invisible to Claude until it re-reads the file.
sheets.lifecycle: Fires after each successful Edit or Write whose path matches, in any session that loads that settings file, and reloads automatically when the file is edited. It stops applying if the hook block is removed, if disableAllHooks is set, or if a managed strictPluginOnlyCustomization or allowManagedHooksOnly policy blocks project-level hooks.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open. PostToolUse runs after the write has already landed and cannot undo it, and a formatter that exits non-zero (anything but 2) only prints a hook error notice while the unformatted edit stands. It also misses files Claude creates through Bash (heredoc, sed, codegen), so pair it with a Stop hook that formats everything git status --porcelain reports if the commit gate must be airtight.
sheets.version_caveat: No version gate on the hook itself. The comma-separated matcher form "Edit,Write" needs Claude Code v2.1.191 or later, and the "if" filter is best-effort: it fails open and runs the hook anyway when the tool input cannot be parsed, so it must not be relied on as the only filter. The practical dependency is jq (or an equivalent JSON parser) existing on every developer machine.

scenarios.scenario: Security mandates that no developer may run the agent with approval prompting switched off entirely, and a developer must not be able to lift the restriction by editing anything in their own home directory or in any repo they control. The control has to hold on every laptop in the fleet.

key.primary: permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode set to "disable" in managed settings deployed to the OS-protected policy location (/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/ on macOS, /etc/claude-code/ on Linux, C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\ on Windows) via MDM or server-managed settings
key.rejected_alternative: Setting the same key in each developer's ~/.claude/settings.json or in the repo's .claude/settings.json
key.rejection_reason: The key works from any scope, but user, project, and local settings files are writable by the developer, who can simply delete the line. Managed settings are the only tier the precedence order says cannot be overridden by any other level, including command-line arguments, and the permissions docs state this key is typically placed in managed settings precisely because it can't be overridden there.
key.context_boundary: no context window at any point (a managed-settings policy key the harness reads at startup to decide which permission modes are selectable); it consumes no conversation context, and nothing the model or a developer-writable file emits can cross back to change it, since managed settings cannot be overridden by anything
key.lifecycle: loaded from the managed policy source at startup (with live reload on change); governs which permission modes are selectable for the whole session
key.failure_mode: The guarantee is only as strong as the OS ACLs on the managed file location and the reach of the deployment tooling: a developer with local admin rights, or a laptop the MDM never touched, is outside the control.

sheets.primary: Managed settings deployed by IT, setting permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode to "disable" (and permissions.disableAutoMode if auto-approval also counts as prompting switched off). Deliver it through a channel the developer cannot write: the macOS com.anthropic.claudecode managed preferences domain via MDM, the Windows HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode registry key via Group Policy or Intune, or /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json and C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json.
sheets.rejected_alternative: The same disableBypassPermissionsMode key in the developer's own ~/.claude/settings.json. It works technically (the key is honored from any scope) but the developer owns that file and can delete the line, which is exactly the loophole being closed.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. Managed settings sit at the top of the precedence chain, above command line arguments and above every user, project and local settings file, so --dangerously-skip-permissions and --permission-mode bypassPermissions are refused at startup.
sheets.context_boundary: Read by the CLI process at startup, entirely outside any context window. Nothing about the policy reaches the model except the practical consequence that permission prompts keep appearing during its tool calls.
sheets.lifecycle: Applies from process start for every session on the enrolled device and re-applies on the settings reload when the policy file changes. It stops applying only when the device leaves management or the policy is removed; there is a bypass_permissions_disabled SessionEnd reason for sessions terminated because the mode was revoked mid-flight.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed on a managed device, but the boundary is the machine and not the person: an unenrolled laptop, a container image, a cloud VM, or a WSL distro without wslInheritsWindowsSettings simply has no policy file and no restriction. On Windows the HKCU policy hive is user-writable and is consulted only when no admin-level source exists, so the HKLM key must actually be deployed or a developer can supply their own policy.
sheets.version_caveat: No minimum version for the key itself, but the legacy Windows path C:\ProgramData\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json stopped being read at v2.1.75 and must be migrated to C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\. Pair it with disableSideloadFlags (v2.1.193 or later) so a single run cannot sideload configuration, and with forceRemoteSettingsRefresh if the policy is delivered by server-managed settings and you need startup to fail closed when the fetch fails.

sheets.primary: A managed enterprise policy settings file deployed by MDM to the system-level location (the ProgramData path on Windows, the /Library/Application Support path on macOS), which sits at the top of the settings precedence chain and pins the permission mode, disabling the bypass-permissions mode outright.
sheets.rejected_alternative: User-level ~/.claude/settings.json, which is exactly what the requirement forbids: it lives in the directory the developer controls and can be edited back.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness, at startup, before the model exists. The policy layer is read by the CLI and cannot be overridden by project or user settings.
sheets.context_boundary: Purely a harness startup concern; the policy file never enters the model context. What the model sees is only the effective permission behaviour, namely that prompts still appear.
sheets.lifecycle: Applies to every session launched on the machine from the moment the file is present, and lapses only when MDM removes or rewrites it, or when the CLI is invoked in a way that does not read the managed path.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed for the ordinary case, but the perimeter is the OS: a developer with local administrator rights can edit the managed file, and the control does not follow the same person into a container, a CI runner, an SDK-embedded agent, or a second unmanaged install. An older CLI that does not recognise the key will ignore it and silently fail open.
sheets.version_caveat: Both the managed-settings path and the specific key that disables the bypass-permissions mode require a recent enough Claude Code; older versions ignore unknown settings keys without warning, which is the dangerous silent-failure case. I cannot state the exact key spelling or minimum version from memory, so pin a minimum version in the fleet image and verify the control empirically on it.

sheets.primary: Managed settings deployed by MDM to every laptop, setting permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode to "disable" (and disableAutoMode alongside it if auto mode is also out of policy). Delivery is the macOS com.anthropic.claudecode managed preferences domain, the Windows HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode registry key, or a system-level managed-settings.json.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A user-level ~/.claude/settings.json carrying the same key. The setting works from any scope, but user settings are the developer's own file, which is exactly the surface the requirement says must not be able to lift the control.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. The permission layer refuses the mode at session start, and the managed scope sits above every other source, so no prompt, no CLAUDE.md, and no CLI flag can restore it.
sheets.context_boundary: None of this reaches the model. It is resolved at CLI startup from the machine's policy chain and applied inside the permission evaluator per tool call; the model only observes that prompts still appear.
sheets.lifecycle: Applied at every session start on that machine and enforced for the whole session, including sessions launched with --dangerously-skip-permissions or --permission-mode bypassPermissions, which are refused. It stops applying only when IT removes or changes the managed policy; a session that was already in bypass mode when the policy arrives ends with SessionEnd reason bypass_permissions_disabled.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed against the intended attack: the flag is rejected and cannot be re-enabled from user or project scope or from the command line. It fails open in two places outside Claude Code's control: a developer with local administrator rights can rewrite the plist, registry value, or managed-settings.json themselves, and with server-managed delivery a failed policy fetch leaves the last-known state unless forceRemoteSettingsRefresh is set to block startup.
sheets.version_caveat: No plan restriction or experimental flag on the setting itself, but the delivery path is version-sensitive: the legacy C:\ProgramData\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json location stopped working in v2.1.75 and must be migrated to C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json. Pair with disableSideloadFlags, which requires v2.1.193 or later, if flag-based side-loading also matters.

sheets.primary: Managed settings deployed by IT (system managed-settings.json, MDM plist or HKLM registry policy, or server managed settings) carrying permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode set to "disable", with disableAutoMode alongside it if silent auto approval also counts as prompting switched off.
sheets.rejected_alternative: The same keys in the project's checked in .claude/settings.json. Rejected because the developer owns that repo and can edit or delete the file; only the managed tier sits outside their reach.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. Managed settings sit above every other source, including command line arguments, so --dangerously-skip-permissions and --permission-mode bypassPermissions are refused rather than negotiated.
sheets.context_boundary: Entirely outside the model's context window. The policy is read by the CLI at startup and shapes the permission engine; the only thing the session sees is the refusal shown to the developer.
sheets.lifecycle: Read at CLI startup on each laptop and in force for the whole session, on every project the developer opens. It stops applying only when IT changes or withdraws the deployed policy.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed on a machine that has the policy, and silently absent on one that never received it, which is where fleet coverage actually breaks. forceRemoteSettingsRefresh is the documented way to make startup fail closed when the policy fetch fails, rather than starting unrestricted.
sheets.version_caveat: On Windows the file must be C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json; the legacy C:\ProgramData\ClaudeCode path stopped being read at v2.1.75, so a stale deployment there enforces nothing. The key itself is honoured from any scope, which is exactly why it has to be placed at the managed tier.
